name: Ağustos Design System
description: Canonical cross-medium design values. CSS, framework adapters, and Office templates are generated consumers.

meta.principle: The website proves the grammar; this registry publishes it.

designDirection.name: İskandivvian
designDirection.definition: Scandinavian restraint filtered through Mediterranean warmth.
designDirection.naming: Use this as a defined project label, not an established design movement.
designDirection.intent: Create minimal, functional, and elegant experiences that feel calm, warm, and human.
principles: Use six colours: white #ffffff as the paper, pale red #fdf5f5 for the closing band, light gray #ebebeb for functional surfaces, dark gray #404040 for secondary text, off-black #15130f for text and buttons, and red #cf142a. Two support values serve only hairlines (#e8e4da) and faint marks (#8a8378). A new value needs a deleted one.

Set type on one golden scale: the 16.5px body times 1.272 per step, so every second step is the golden ratio (13, 16.5, 21, 27, 34, 43, 55, 70, 89px). Headings are thin: hero 89px light, H1 55px light, H2 43px regular, H3 21px medium. Use four weights (300, 400, 500, 600). The wordmark alone uses 650.
Use two radii, 6px for controls and 12px for cards, and one section spacing. Do not use gradients or textures. The only shadow sits under a menu that floats above the page.

Red is identity and signal, never action: the logo, the 2px link and menu rule, keyboard focus, and one highlighter stroke per page. Buttons are black. The Ağustos logo is red and turns black on hover; every other house brand's logo is black and turns red on hover.

Use the highlighter on one to four words of the main headline: once on the homepage, at most once on any other page. Never on links, buttons, numbers, body text, or product UI. The sentence must read the same without it.

Websites use the top menu with at most five items. Extra pages go under one More menu, and social, legal, and language links live in the footer. Product UI uses the sidebar, or the top menu when it has about ten destinations or fewer. Every page starts light. A site may add a theme switch; the user picks dark, never the device.
Copy a screen; do not design a page. Open with a headline, a deck, two buttons, and a trust line. Close with one pale red band.

Bold (600) marks a fact the reader scans for, at most once per paragraph. Italic marks names of publications and projects, foreign terms, and quoted phrases. Underline is for links only. Do not combine them, and do not use uppercase labels, eyebrow headings, or coloured text.
When unsure, do the conventional thing. Collect design tweaks and release the kit once a month; fix real defects at once.

invariants.rule: One symbol and a lowercase wordmark in the identity ink. Never redrawn, never with a tagline.
invariants.web: The site lockup in the top menu and the footer.
invariants.datasheet: The lockup at the top left of every sheet.
invariants.linkedin: The lockup at the foot of every post image; the avatar is the symbol tile.

invariants.rule: Red is identity and signal only: the Ağustos logo, and on screen the link rule, focus and one marker stroke. Never a fill, a button or text colour.
invariants.web: The logo, the 2px link and menu rule, keyboard focus and one highlighter stroke per page. Buttons are black.
invariants.datasheet: No red, except the Ağustos logo.
invariants.linkedin: No red, except the Ağustos logo and at most one highlighter stroke in the headline.

invariants.rule: Three faces on one scale: Inter Tight for headings, Inter for text, JetBrains Mono for data. Headings are thin and in sentence case.
invariants.web: The type table (recipes.typeRoles) through the kit classes.
invariants.datasheet: The same faces and weights at the print sizes of recipes.document.
invariants.linkedin: The headline takes the H1 role, the deck the deck role.

invariants.rule: Spec values are data: mono figures with the unit, the label in the display face.
invariants.web: type-spec on the spec table or list.
invariants.linkedin: Any figure that appears in a post image.

invariants.rule: White paper and generous space. One title opens the page and nothing sits above it.
invariants.web: White paper, the section spacing, one closing band.
invariants.datasheet: White A4, wide margins, one product title.
invariants.linkedin: A white field; the headline is the only large text.

invariants.rule: Plain, short, active words. No all-caps labels, no label above a title, no inflated claims.
invariants.web: Sentence case in headings, menus and buttons.
invariants.datasheet: Sentence case labels; Turkish with lang=tr.
invariants.linkedin: One idea per post image, in sentence case.

invariants.rule: Text clears 4.5:1 contrast and graphics 3:1 (WCAG 2.2 AA).
invariants.web: The states table; the build refuses a failing pair.
invariants.datasheet: Ink and ink-soft on white only.
invariants.linkedin: Ink on white only; no text on a photograph.

avoid: Red buttons, red statistics, red fills, or red text. The logo and the one highlighter stroke are the only red areas
More than one highlighter stroke on a page
Uppercase labels, eyebrow labels, arrows on buttons, or decorative motion
Inflated luxury claims or forced friendliness
A primary button in every section, card, or list
A sidebar on a website, or more than five items in its top menu
A theme that follows the device setting, or a page that starts dark
Lifestyle photography or a photograph behind body text
acceptance: Pages feel calm, warm, and complete through white paper, thin headings on one scale, and helpful language.
Visitors can understand the content and identify the next action quickly.
Red appears only as identity and signal: the logo, link and menu rules, focus, and at most one highlighter stroke.
Every page starts light, only the user switches it to dark, and the top menu fits in five items.
Forms and technical content remain clear, readable, and easy to scan.
Brand identity, keyboard focus, reduced motion, and supported themes remain intact.

paperCream.$description: Full-bleed callout and CTA band. Logo red at 5% into white. Never the page paper.

paperWhite.$description: Primary substrate. About 70% of every surface.

paperGray.$description: Functional surfaces: key-figure tiles, image regions, and summary panels.

ink.$description: Headlines, filled buttons, footer, and house-brand identity ink.

inkFaint.$description: Non-content marks only: form field borders, disabled state, separators. It scores 3.75:1 on white, below the 4.5:1 text floor. Support value, not a seventh palette colour.

ruleCream.$description: Hairline rule on light surfaces. Support value, not a seventh palette colour.

ruleWhite.$description: Hairline rule alias kept for compatibility.

paperDark.$description: Dark paper. Reuses off-black. No new hex.

inkDark.$description: Primary text on dark. Reuses white. No new hex.

inkSoftDark.$description: Secondary text on dark. Reuses the faint-label support value.

inkFaintDark.$description: Quiet text on dark. Same hex as inkSoftDark. No new hex.

ruleDark.$description: Separator on dark. Reuses dark gray. No new hex.

creamDark.$description: Light gray callout in the dark theme, used for identity tiles. The closing band takes the dark paper instead (v7.7.0). Reuses light gray. No new hex.

surfaceDark.$description: Dark cards and panels. Reuses dark gray. No new hex.

signalRed.$description: Shared Ağustos-family interaction signal for links, focus, markers, and small emphasis across every brand.

stateSuccessDark.$description: Positive system feedback on the dark substrate.

stateWarningDark.$description: Caution system feedback on the dark substrate.

stateDangerDark.$description: Destructive or failed system feedback on the dark substrate.

stateInfoDark.$description: Informational system feedback on the dark substrate.

display.$description: Wordmarks, heroes, headings, labels, and designed UI.

mono.$description: Code, identifiers, units, and technical values.

fontSize.$description: One golden scale: 16.5px times 1.272 (the square root of the golden ratio) per step, so every second step is 1.618. Steps: 13, 16.5, 21, 27, 34, 43, 55, 70, 89px. Headings shrink one or two steps on small screens. Two sizes are off the scale: bodyCompact for menus, buttons, tables and the hero trust line, and formField, the smallest input size that stops a phone from zooming.

heroMedium.$description: Alias of h1, kept for compatibility.

pullquote.$description: Pull quote. The step between H3 and H2.

formField.$description: Text inputs. A phone zooms into a field below 16px.

footnote.$description: Footnotes, captions, code blocks and breadcrumbs.

lineHeight.$description: Line height per type role. Large type sets tight, reading text sets open.

letterSpacing.$description: Tracking per heading role. Large display type tightens; body text keeps the font's own spacing.

medium.$description: Controls: buttons, inputs, badges, menu items.

large.$description: Cards, bands with corners, and floating menus.

content.$description: Shared content column for page and chrome.

body.$description: The reading line: long-form text, and the line between the main zone and the side zone. 656px, about 75 characters of Inter at 16.5px. In rem, so every element puts the line in the same place.

wide.$description: Media and data width. Same as the content column.

controlMinimum.$description: Minimum button-like target on the shorter axis.

states.$description: Every interactive state in both themes, as foreground and background keys from foundations.color. The build rejects a pair below its floor: text 4.5:1, graphics (borders, logos, focus) 3:1; disabled controls are exempt. Red stays the signal: in the dark theme a hover dims the ink instead of turning it red. The footer and the closing band follow the theme; the dark band is the dark paper between two hairline rules. Pressed buttons move 1px down. Disabled controls are gray and do not react. tokens/web.css.tmpl implements these rows.

rows.element: Keyboard focus ring in the closing band

drawerWidth.$description: Sidebar and topbar drawers from 640px to 1023px. Below 640px a drawer covers the whole width.

breadcrumbEnd.$description: The gap between the breadcrumb and the title below it.

metaGap.$description: The gap between the deck and the meta line under it (date, author, revision).

breadcrumbStart.$description: A page that opens with a breadcrumb: the trail sits this far under the top menu, not the full hero padding.

paddingBlockEnd.$description: Small on purpose: the first section below brings the section spacing.

paddingBlock.$description: The one section spacing. Sections, the closing band, and the gap after the hero all use it.

heading.$description: Vertical rhythm around headings, in fixed steps. The space above a heading is larger than the space below it, so the heading binds to the text it opens.

afterTitle.$description: Below a hero headline or an H1: the title-to-deck gap.

social.$description: LinkedIn post images. Text uses the type table at one scale factor, so a post reads like the website seen from arm's length. One idea per image: a headline, a deck, at most four spec values, and the lockup at the foot.

scale.$description: Multiplies each type role's largest size; a feed shows the image at about half its width.

typeRoles.$description: The type contract, one row per role. Every medium reads this table: the web kit, UI-KIT.md, the brand guidelines and the LinkedIn templates. Sizes, weights and spaces point at foundation tokens.

hero.use: The one headline of a home or landing page. One per page.
hero.avoid: A second hero on the page; a hero on a content page (use H1).

h1.use: The title of every page that has no hero. One per page.
h1.avoid: Two H1s; an H1 inside a card.

deck.use: One or two sentences directly under the hero or the H1 that say what the page is.
deck.avoid: A deck under an H2; more than two sentences.

h2.avoid: A label above the heading; uppercase.

h3.use: A subsection, or the title of a card.
h3.avoid: Italic; bold to fake an H2.

h4.use: A small group title: a table caption, a footer group, a form group.
h4.avoid: An eyebrow label above a heading; uppercase.

body.use: All running text. 1em below each paragraph.
body.avoid: A line longer than the reading line (--measure-body); grey text below 4.5:1.

compact.use: Tables and the hero trust line.

control.use: Buttons at 600. Menu links and breadcrumbs at 500; breadcrumbs take the footnote size.

quote.use: A quotation inside the text, in italic with a 2px ink rule.
quote.avoid: Decorative quote marks; a quote as a section heading.

pullquote.use: One line lifted from a long article.

footnote.use: Footnotes, image captions and code blocks.
footnote.avoid: Any text the reader needs to act on.

spec.use: Product specification values with units (160 W, 4200 lm). The label stays in the display face. The same on the web, the datasheet and LinkedIn.

screens.$description: One reference composition per page type. Files live under screens/. Every screen starts light; the user may switch it to dark. Chrome follows family: every website family uses the top menu and the footer; product-ui uses the sidebar, or the top menu when its row says chrome topbar (about ten destinations or fewer).

home.purpose: The homepage: a thin headline with one highlighter stroke, a deck, two buttons and a trust line, then the brand and software card sections, and one closing pale red band.
home.photo: one installation photograph, third in the rollout

static.purpose: The static page template: About, privacy, terms, and the KVKK notice. Intro, timeline, and people in the reading column on the left edge of the frame.
static.photo: people and places that explain the work

content.purpose: One article or post: title, deck, long-form body at the reading line with headings, lists, a quote, and a footnote.
content.photo: only when it explains the content

content-index.purpose: The list of posts: one section per year, body-size title links with a footnote line each, newest first. No heading per title.

landing.purpose: A page that makes several arguments in a row, such as a service page: one argument per section (who it is for, problem, method, role, cost, proof), a section gap between them, each picture in the side zone to the right of the text, and one closing pale red band.
landing.photo: a photograph or a drawing that adds information; one width for every picture

products.purpose: The product listing: an H1 page title, series sections with product cards, quick links, and one closing pale red band.
products.photo: product thumbnails, second in the rollout

product-finder.purpose: The product finder: a filter column and a result list. Form submits are task actions, not the page primary.
product-finder.photo: product thumbnails, second in the rollout

product.purpose: One luminaire: photograph and drawing, description, grouped specification tables, downloads, and related products.
product.photo: product photograph or drawing, first in the rollout

spec-sheet.purpose: The A4 technical datasheet (teknik föy) as a web page: header, photograph and drawing, the five specification groups, revision line.

app-shell.purpose: The product-UI frame: sidebar navigation with counts, a page toolbar, stats, and a data table. The theme switch lives in the sidebar.

app-top-menu.purpose: A small product on the top menu: grouped Tools, a list of the user's files, the theme switch and the account list at the end, and the footer. For a product with about ten destinations or fewer.
